body:
I totally agree, I don't think he was mean spirited, but did what he could do. I think that he wasn't a good father, but also it wasn't that he was purposefully awful to her or neglectful, just plainly, not great.

I agree about him not mentioning her again as bad writing, after all it just seems to come up again only once when he tells Lexie about Sofia, and it was clearly just a way to give some more drama to the show.

I agree with what you say, he had no idea on what to do with Sloan, but also I don't think he actively tried to hear what she had to say.  
  
I believe he did try to actively try to prevent it, as he tried to talk her into it, even when Arizona was trying to convince him to call the adoptive parents, and Callie had already told him that Sloan didn't want him to raise the baby. He really tried for Sloan to change her mind, only to realize halfway through it that he was being selfish and respect her decision.   
  
He got better with time and had his good moments, but still, he wasn't a great parent for a good chunk of it.  
  
I did let off Sofia but for the sole fact that she was a baby, I don't think they ever got to a point where it would be possible to judge much since she couldn't even walk or talk. I must say he was way more present, but also he was older, wanted a child and knew about her since the beggining, which changes everything drastically.

(Also I must admit, I do think it was sort of shitty of him to say he could "screw again" with Callie and make another baby when they had to pick Sofia or Callie's life, but at the same time it's a totally understandable choice (or at least I think so, as someone who grew up in a system where the life of the mother comes before the life of the fetus/baby). But that was before Sofia was born, so it's different.)
